name: NY-14
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 19 points on partisan baseline
Ocasio-Cortez holds a massive money edge: $17.4 million on hand versus about $31,000 for Hysenaj
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent
No outside spending against the incumbent and no signs of serious Republican investment in the seat
model.rationale: The district's 19-point Democratic lean, Ocasio-Cortez's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent all point to a comfortable hold, and no evidence on the other side suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national swing toward Republicans or an unforeseen development involving the incumbent could narrow this, and nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez seeks reelection in a New York City district that leans Democratic by 19 points. She has raised more than $37 million this cycle and holds $17.4 million on hand, while Republican Diamant Hysenaj has raised about $343,000 with roughly $31,000 remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets put her chances at about 97 percent.

No public polls cover the general election, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. Those signals align on a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
